newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude gains, Brent sales dampen sweets.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude gains, Brent sales dampen sweets.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes rallied sharply Friday afternoon on technically-inspired buying on the NYMEX futures market, pushing prompt crude prices through key chart points above $21.50 a barrel.
At 1354 EDT/1754 GMT, June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was around 40 cents higher at $21.65-75 a barrel, steady to two cents weaker than July quotes.
At the same time outright values advanced, the price paid for domestic grade differentials steadied in light volume.
Traders said the latest numbers in the grade sector had Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sold at three cents under marker WTI, steady with prices paid on Thursday.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire sold at 68 cents under June WTI/Cushing, 20 cents weaker than Wednesday, but even with talked ranges late Thursday.
Midland/WTI traded at 37 cents below June WTI/Cushing, unchanged from Thursday.
Sweet grades have grown bearish in the later stages of this week's action, depressed by wide arbitrage spreads against Brent barrels, opening the Gulf for foreign shipments.
"At these numbers, you should be able to bring Brent over all day," said one cash broker.
A U.S. trade house sold Brent into the Gulf late Thursday, furthering the pressure on sweet domestics.

On the sour side of the market, West Texas Sour/Midland sold at $1.38 under WTI, a few pennies stronger than late Thursday. Eugene Island also moved, in small volumes, at a $1.60 discount, traders said.
WTI/Cushing Postings Plus sold at $2.05, five cents improved from the morning and steady with Thursday.
